opening_message:
Ticket 1: Edward Fleming (employee ID E042) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E042.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Edward Fleming (E042) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin requires owning the system (Engineer role), which does not apply here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E042 is a contractor with basic training (note says full-time, but security record takes precedence). Contractors max is read without advanced training; requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Edward Fleming (E042) requested write access to Source Code. The security record (which takes precedence per the team note) identifies E042 as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training; basic training means the maximum is read. Since the requested write exceeds the allowed maximum, grant the maximum of read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee E042 (Edward Fleming) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes with conflicting information:
- Note 1 (HR): role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommendation write.
- Note 2 (Security): role Payroll Specialist, employment type contractor, security training basic, recommendation read. Security note says security record takes precedence.

So we have conflicting employment type: full_time vs contractor. The security note says security record takes precedence.

Policy:
- full_time: up to write, admin only if role owns system. Source Code is owned by Engineer. Payroll Specialist doesn't own. So max write.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin. Security training is basic, so max read.

Given security says contractor with basic training, max is read. Requested write is above max, so grant max = read.

The security note explicitly says security record takes precedence. So grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.
